title: How to Fast
excerpt: Fasting is not a hunger strike against God to make him answer. It is the deliberate emptying of the body to remind the soul what it actually hungers for.
body:
Fasting is the discipline most Christians believe in and almost never practice. We affirm it in theory, file it under "things serious believers do," and then live decades without ever doing it. Part of this is fear, part is confusion, and part is that we live in a culture that treats any voluntary discomfort as a kind of madness. But Jesus assumed his followers would fast. He did not say "if you fast." He said "when you fast." It was not optional in his mind. It should not be invisible in ours.

## Understand what it is for

Fasting is going without food, or some other good thing, for a set time, in order to seek God. That is the simple definition. The deeper purpose is exposure. When you remove food, the thing that keeps your body comfortable and distracted, you discover quickly how much you have been using comfort to keep God at arm's length. The hunger pang becomes a prompt. Every time the stomach growls, the soul is reminded to turn toward the One it actually needs.

Fasting is not a hunger strike to force God's hand. He is not moved by our discomfort the way a parent is moved by a tantrum. Nor is it a diet with a spiritual coat of paint. It is a way of saying, with the body and not just the lips, that we hunger for God more than for bread. Jesus, after forty days without food, told the tempter exactly that. Man does not live by bread alone.

## Start small and concrete

Do not begin with forty days. Begin with one meal. Skip lunch, and spend the time you would have eaten in prayer instead. That is a real fast, and it will teach you more than reading ten articles about fasting. From there you might try one full day, sunup to sundown, taking only water. Build slowly, the way you would build any difficult thing.

Be concrete about the boundaries before you start. What are you giving up, water only or also juice, for how long, and what will you do with the time and the hunger. A fast without a plan tends to collapse into simply being grumpy and missing lunch. Decide in advance that every hunger pang is a call to prayer, and the discomfort becomes fuel instead of distraction.

## Replace the meal with prayer, not with nothing

The point of fasting is not the empty stomach. It is the full attention you give to God in the space the food used to occupy. If you skip lunch and spend the hour scrolling your phone, you have dieted, not fasted. Take the time you would have spent eating and pray, read Scripture, sit in silence. The hunger is meant to drive you toward God, not merely away from food.

## Keep it hidden

Jesus was blunt about this. When you fast, do not advertise it. Do not walk around looking weary so people will admire your devotion. Wash your face, go about your day, and let the fast be a secret between you and your Father. The moment fasting becomes a performance, it stops forming the soul and starts feeding the ego, which is the very thing it was supposed to starve.

This is hard, because we want credit for hard things. But the hiddenness is part of the medicine. A fast no one knows about can only be for God, and that is exactly the point.

## Expect it to surface ugly things

When you take away food, you will be surprised by what comes up. Irritability. A short temper. A craving so loud it shocks you. This is not the fast going wrong. This is the fast working. It is showing you how much of your peace was propped up by comfort and full meals. The irritation you feel at hour twenty is data about your heart. Bring it to God instead of taking it out on the people near you.

## A word of caution

Fasting is a discipline of the body, and bodies differ. If you are pregnant or nursing, if you are diabetic, if you have a history of an eating disorder, if you are on medication that requires food, do not fast from food without talking to a doctor first. There are other things to fast from, screens, news, sugar, that carry the same spiritual purpose without the physical risk. Fasting is meant to humble the body, not to harm it. Wisdom here is not weakness. It is faithfulness.

## This week

Pick one day. On that day, skip one meal, lunch is easiest, and drink only water. When the hunger comes, and it will, let it move you to pray, even one sentence: "Lord, I want you more than I want this." At the end of the day, write down one thing the hunger revealed about where your comfort really comes from. Tell no one.

The body learns what the mind forgets. Let your stomach preach to your soul.
